the dorsal raphe nucleus contains a large number of estrogen receptor‐containing cells that are not serotonin neurons.

The main takeaway from our work is that
estrogen receptors and proestrogen receptors are found in nonserotonergic neurons in the dorsal raphe nucleus, and that these receptors are induced by estrogen.
the steroid hormone estradiol has a direct and powerful effect on the activity of the brain chemical serotonin.
estrogen and progestin can modulate serotonin activity via nonserotonergic neurons in the dorsal raphe.
